metadata.title: CAT 2026 historical QA allocation study
metadata.studyType: Retrospective chronological reconstruction assembled after the historical outcomes were known.
metadata.scope: The selector scores QA family counts. The diagnostics block separately scores a damped-trend rule, a slot-noise floor, Verbal Ability type mix and DILR set layout. Section totals remain descriptive metadata.

indore2020.note: Section totals read directly from Cracku slot pages (VARC 26, DILR 24, QA 26). No reliable 2020 topic table was recovered: the only one found did not sum to 26 per slot, so it is not used.

limitations: No archived pre-exam publication of these predictions is claimed.
Each exam year in 2021-2025 had a different convening IIM, so a setter-specific style cannot be estimated; IIM Indore's last CAT (2020) used a different 76-question format.

The official CAT 2026 mock repeats the 2025 mock and, by its own note, is not meant to reveal the 2026 pattern; it confirms format rules only. Scored on 2025, that mock missed the Verbal Ability mix and the TITA count.
Rows added in v4.0 other than 2022 Slot 1 were read from IMS page content in search results, not opened directly.
Rules and source selection were assembled retrospectively; chronological computation does not remove retrospective design choices.
Slots within a year are correlated, coverage is incomplete, and the evaluation contains only a few target years.
Topic-count overlap is an allocation similarity measure, not the percentage of exact exam questions predicted.
Observed ranges and maximum historical errors are descriptive, not calibrated confidence or prediction intervals.
No exact-paper guarantee, question-match probability, difficulty forecast, percentile prediction or individual paper-author inference is supplied.
sourceNotes: The primary model uses thirteen complete IMS QA reports from 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025: 286 reported question allocations, not 286 independent predictions. Evaluation targets are 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. No calendar year inside the covered span is missing.

v4.0 added five rows (2022 Slots 1 and 3, 2023 Slots 1-3). Only 2022 Slot 1 was opened directly. The others were read from IMS page content in search results because direct IMS URLs returned 404 or 410, the same access limit already noted for 2022 Slot 2 and 2024. These rows are less verified than directly opened pages.

2023 Slot 2 has two conflicting IMS tables: overall page Geometry 2 / Modern Math 3, slot article Geometry 3 / Modern Math 2. The overall table is primary and the other is a sensitivity row, as for 2025 Slot 1. Under the alternative, the raw selector changes its 2026 choice, so treat the raw 2026 split as sensitive to this single cell.

2021 Slot 1 is excluded because IMS lists no Numbers row (the four stated counts sum to 22). No implicit zero is inserted under this strict complete-explicit-cell rule. 2022 Slots 1 and 3 are now included; see above.

2024 Slot 3 stays excluded. IMS overall table leaves Modern Math blank; the slot page table (8/7/3/1/3 with Modern Math 3) equals the Slot 1 vector, while its narrative gives Algebra 5. Copy error cannot be ruled out, so no value is used.

Career Launcher 2023 counts differ from IMS 2023 counts (for example Slot 1 9/8/3/1/1 against 7/8/4/1/2). Providers classify borderline questions differently, so a count error of about one question per category is classification noise before any forecasting error.

Taxonomy remains uncertain even within one provider. The 2022 report places functions, logarithms and progressions in Modern Math, while some later descriptions place functions in Algebra. Combining Algebra and Modern Math reduces this known boundary issue but does not establish complete question-level consistency.
Geometry is not fixed at 3: 2022 Slot 3 and 2023 Slot 1 report 4, and the 2023 Slot 2 overall table reports 2. It is the steadiest family, not a constant.

Every CAT in 2021-2025 was convened by a different IIM, so each setter appears once and no setter-specific style can be estimated. IIM Indore last convened CAT in 2020, in a 76-question pandemic format that is not comparable to the current 68-question format.

Source pages were inspected in September and November 2026; some historical articles were available only through indexed provider content while direct URLs returned errors. Source links may therefore fail. No archived pre-exam snapshot is claimed. Detailed recovery notes are saved in research-2021-2022.json and research-2023-2024.json.

Small, incomplete modern-format coverage can bias the study toward stable structure. The model does not analyse every paper since 1991, infer the authors of individual questions, estimate exam difficulty, or predict exact future question text. No calibrated confidence interval, percentile or question-match probability is provided.

DILR arrays are sorted set-size multisets, not the source’s set order or topic frequencies. VARC arrays are [RC, summary, sentence placement, odd sentence, parajumbles]. Rows without varc or dilr fields (2023 Slots 1 and 3, 2023 Slot 2 VARC) are skipped by the VARC and DILR studies, not imputed.

Official CAT 2026 mock (released 6 November 2026): its instructions give 24/22/22 questions, 40 minutes per section, four questions per RC passage, four or five questions per DILR set and whole-number TITA answers. With 22 DILR questions, sets of four or five allow only one layout, 5/5/4/4/4. The mock-link PDF states the 120-minute, 40-per-section timing for CAT 2026 itself.

The 2026 official mock repeats the 2025 official mock question for question, in a new order. Scored against the real 2025 paper, the 2025 mock got the section counts and DILR layout right (as did simply repeating 2024) but not the Verbal Ability mix (3/3/2/0 against 2/2/2/2) or the TITA count (20 against 23). The 2026 mock therefore confirms format rules but carries no new information about CAT 2026 topics.
TITA counts per section come from IMS for 2025 only (4/11/8 in all three slots). The 2026 TITA forecast repeats 2025; one 2024 slot report gives 2/10/8, so 20 to 23 is the recent range.

modelSettings.rawToBroad: Merge Algebra and Modern Math; retain Arithmetic, Geometry and Numbers.
modelSettings.trainingCutoff: For each target year, use primary rows with year strictly less than target year.
modelSettings.foldDefinition: Each observed year after the first is one target fold; missing years do not create folds or imputed rows.
modelSettings.withinYearWeighting: Equal mean of available slots in each training year.
modelSettings.comparisonAggregation: Equal mean over target-year metric values, not a pooled average over all historical slots.

methods.name: Last-year baseline
methods.rule: Mean of the latest available year’s slots.

methods.name: Equal-year history
methods.rule: Mean of yearly means; every training year gets equal weight.

methods.name: Recency, 2-year half-life
methods.rule: Yearly means weighted by 2^((year − latest year)/2).

methods.name: Fixed three-rule ensemble
methods.rule: Equal average of last-year, equal-year and recency forecasts.

methods.name: Uniform null baseline
methods.rule: 22/5 for each original family, then merge if using broad groups.

selector.objective: Lowest mean target-year MAE among completed earlier folds only.

metrics.mae: Mean absolute difference between forecast and actual question counts across topic cells within a target year.
metrics.overlapPercent: 100 * (1 - absolute_count_error / (2 * target_slots * 22)). Averaged equally over target years in summaries.
metrics.exact: Cells with absolute error below 1e-9. Summaries sum exact counts and evaluated cells across target folds.
metrics.maxHistoricalErrors: Largest absolute error by family in the selector predictions for historical target slots; not a future bound.

modelSettings.rounding: Only displayed integer scenarios are rounded. Largest remainders preserve 22 questions; ties follow displayed family order. All evaluation scores use unrounded forecasts.

2026.sameEvidence: Same four RC passage IDs, same five DILR set IDs and sizes, same text-length and image fingerprint for all 22 QA questions, same MCQ/TITA counts; only the order is shuffled.
officialStatements: The mock-link PDF says CAT 2026 has 120 minutes for non-PwBD candidates, 40 minutes per section.
The same PDF says the mock uses selected questions from previous CAT papers and is not meant to reveal the CAT 2026 pattern; counts and timing in the mock are indicative.
The 4 Nov 2026 media release says the test is on 29 November 2026 in three shifts, with admit cards from 6 November.
Disputes fall under the CAT Centre 2026 in Indore, and the help desk uses an iimidr.ac.in address, which supports IIM Indore as convenor.
